item.title: The School of Athens
item.lesson: While Michelangelo painted the Sistine ceiling a few rooms away, the twenty-six-year-old Raphael frescoed the pope's private library with the entire history of Greek philosophy gathered in one imaginary marble hall. At the center walk Plato and Aristotle: Plato points up toward the world of ideal forms, Aristotle gestures flat toward the earth and its particulars — the two directions of Western thought in two hands. Raphael cast his contemporaries in the roles: Plato wears Leonardo da Vinci's face, and the brooding figure slumped on the steps in front, Heraclitus, is Michelangelo — added at the last minute, in Michelangelo's own painting style, after Raphael sneaked a look at the unfinished Sistine ceiling. It is the High Renaissance summarized: classical learning, perfect perspective, and a young artist confident enough to paint philosophy itself.
item.lookFor: At the far right edge, the young man in a dark cap looking straight out at you is Raphael himself, quietly attending the greatest faculty meeting ever assembled.
